steps.title: Lesson 2: Core Concepts
steps.body: Key Fact: Representation in UK film is shaped by the specific social, cultural and political dynamics of British society, where class, region, ethnicity and national identity intersect in distinctive ways. | Key Fact: Class representation is central to British cinema in ways that have no direct equivalent in Hollywood, with social realism making working-class experience a primary rather than marginal subject. | Key Fact: Regional identity representation challenges the London-centric bias of British media, giving voice to the cultures, dialects and experiences of Scotland, Wales, Northern Ireland and England's regions. | Key Fact: Ethnic representation in UK film has evolved from near-invisibility through stereotyping towards greater complexity, though significant under-representation and t
